Resolves #21602

The hero's strip now says what it is. A moving scene's caption opens "Replay of 13–19 Nov 2026" and counts "180 of 301 merged pull requests"; the legend ends with a warm stroke and "136 change requests", so the scene's one warm mark has a word and the number stands once; the merge seat reads "@tobiu merges". The strip's words are drawn at the dim ink's full strength. The replay's clock beside the running day ends before the next day's name at every width: with its zone, without it, or left out.

Evidence: L2 (the hero rendered in the dev Portal: frames in both themes at five sizes, the clock's row at four more, a contrast read from PNG pixels, the e2e spec at three sizes, one blind read) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-9, AC-11). Residual: AC-10's sentence in the guide, Residual-Owner: #21580.

Review focus: (1) the wording, as a stranger reads it: does "Replay of … · 180 of 301 merged pull requests" still leave room for the merge-rate reading? (2) `captionOf`'s order: what a square is now goes before a part of the record's caption does. (3) the engine writes two more English words ("Replay of", "merges") beside the ones it already wrote ("Contributors", "merged", "reviewed by").

Prescription checked: `src/canvas/RoundTable.mjs` owns the concern. Only the scene knows whether it is moving or still, it defines what kind `merge` and a `'C'` review mean, and `captionOf` composes the caption. `buildScripts/docs/recordWeek.mjs` owns the record's words, so the unit changes there. This ticket was authored in the session that built it, so that question is the reviewer's to answer.

## Deltas from ticket

- **AC-7 named no measure, and the first measurement showed why it needs one.** WCAG compares the text's colour with its ground: that reading stood at 4.30:1 in the light theme, because the strip's words were drawn at 0.9 of the dim ink. They are now drawn at 1. The ticket's criterion is sharpened in its body (17:41Z).
- **The legend's words take the same strength**, since one line of `drawStrip` sets it for both.
- **AC-11 came after the pull request opened**, from the home steward's defect note on a 768 px frame: the running day's clock was drawn over the next day's label. It is the same function and the same row, so it is fixed here (`2ba824f915`) and the criterion stands in the ticket's body.
- **Not done, on purpose:** a heavier weight for the strip's words. Tried at 600: the glyph cores rose from 3.95:1 to 4.07:1 in the light theme and the strip looked heavier. Reverted.

## Test Evidence

**Contrast, from the rendered frame.** A PNG of the caption's row at 1440 × 900, twelve seconds in, decoded on a page canvas. Ground: the clip's most frequent colour. "Colour" is the palette's dim ink at the scene's alpha over that ground, which is what WCAG compares. "Glyph cores" is the mean of the pixels in the upper half of the distance from the ground, so what the rasteriser leaves of 12 px text.

| Theme | Ground | Colour, before | Colour, now | Glyph cores, before | Glyph cores, now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neo-dark | rgb(25, 32, 50) | 5.03:1 | **5.87:1** | 4.08:1 | 4.73:1 |
| neo-light | rgb(247, 249, 254) | 4.30:1 | **5.34:1** | 3.33:1 | 3.95:1 |

The light theme's glyph cores stay under 4.5:1. That is anti-aliasing on thin text, and the lever would be the light palette's `inkDim` in the Portal's host, which also colours the day names and the cards: not this leaf.

**Frames.** The released hero (`origin/dev`, a detached worktree) beside this branch, each in a fresh context.

In each pair the released hero is above and this branch below, at 1440 × 900, 1:1.

**The clock's row.** The form is chosen once per layout, so it does not come and go while a day's count gains a digit. Measured in the scene's font (500 12px `system-ui`, on a canvas in Chromium): the widest day name is 42.6 px, the fullest count ("69") 15.7 px, "00:00 UTC" 63.1 px and "00:00" 34.8 px. With the gaps the row draws (7 and 9) and 9 px before the next name, the whole clock needs a strip of 1,007 px and the short one a strip of 809 px.

| Window | Strip | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 768 × 1024 | 736 px | over "Wed 18" | no clock |
| 900 × 700 | 868 px | runs into "Wed 18" | "22:45" |
| 1024 × 768 | 992 px | ends 7 px before the next name at the widest day | "22:45" |
| 1280 × 800 | 1,024 px | fits | "22:05 UTC", unchanged |

## Cold look

One reader with no context (a helper given only the unlabelled frames: version A the released hero, version B this branch; two and twelve seconds in, both themes, the phone, and each desktop frame's bottom at full size). It answered for A before it opened B. Its quotes are checked against the frames.

| | Released | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| The caption, in its words | "180 of 301 pull requests were merged" | "a playback of a past week"; 180 is "how many of the week's 301 merged pull requests have been shown so far" |
| The two empty days | "a stranger could just as well read them as days with no merged pull requests" | "the replay has not reached those days yet, rather than that nothing happened" |
| The warm lines | "nothing for … change requests, which exist only as words" | "a different kind of mark, a line rather than a square, and it matches the orange streak" |
| The merge seat | "I cannot tell what it does" | "a person, @tobiu, doing the merging … the gate the squares pass through" |
| "I understand what this picture shows and where its numbers come from" | 6 of 10 | 8 of 10 |

Asked last and directly whether either version suggested that only part of the pull requests were accepted: the released one yes ("so 121 were not"), this branch "mostly no".

**What the reader still misses, in its order, and what becomes of it:**

1. The two days stay blank with no "not yet" mark, so at twelve seconds they can still be read as days without work. Not changed: the reader's own conclusion was the right one, so the ticket's condition for dimming them further did not arise. The lever is one constant, the alpha of a day name the replay has not reached.
2. The clock beside the current day is not labelled as the replay's, and nothing says that it loops. Not changed.
3. The legend says "Contributors" and the caption "outside contributors". A real mismatch between the scene's word and the generator's; out of scope here, noted for the next touch of the legend.
4. "@tobiu merges" does not say that every square passes that seat. The seat's card says it ("merged 301 pull requests"); at rest it stays unsaid.
5. At 1440 px "one square each" is gone, so what a square is must be inferred from the day totals. That is the order this ticket chose; from about 1,480 px the words return.

It also noted that the names on the ring are unexplained and that the headline rotates to a phrase that fits neither the picture nor the sentence: both are the copy leaf's (#21595).
